data.claim: Reviewer selection has no declared priority: within the cross-family tier the gate runs reviewers in config order only. A priority field on the reviewer (lower served first) reorders that pool within the same independence tier.
data.falsifier: Two cross-family reviewers, priorities 10 and 90, config lists the 90 first: fixed code runs the 10 first; unfixed keeps config order, or Reviewer(priority=10) raises TypeError.
data.mechanism: _order_cross_family_first sorts by review_tier rank alone (a stable sort), so two cross-family reviewers keep config order whatever a declared priority says, and the Reviewer dataclass rejects an unknown priority field.
data.probe: python3: Reviewer(priority=10) and _order_cross_family_first([later(90), first(10)]) with a deepseek author and Config()
data.probe_output: pre-fix TypeError unknowkwarg priority and order later,first; post-fix default 100 and order first,middle,later
data.question: Is reviewer priority only the implicit registry order, so a declared priority field is needed?

evidence.note: probe: Reviewer(priority=10) pre-fix TypeError (unknown kwarg) then lower-first ordering within the family tier; post-fix default 100 and order [first(10),middle(50),later(90)], cross-family still dominating priority, ties keeping config order (tests/test_reviewer_priority.py, 5 passed).
research R4876b3c5b7 CONFIRMED: declared priority orders a gate's pool within the cross-family tier (lower first); tests/test_reviewer_priority.py 5 passed, reviewer regression selection 52 passed.

ddflow brief --item RV-reviewer-priority loaded: rules digest includes r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY before gemini reviews), r-docs-with-the-change, r-everything-configurable, r-reviewer-independence constraints; reviewed _order_cross_family_first and reviewer_trust.IDENTITY (priority is a tuning knob, not an identity field, so tuning it needs no re-approval).

Added priority=100 to Reviewer (lower served first) and ranked the gate pool by (cross-family tier, priority) in _order_cross_family_first; documented the [[reviewer]] priority knob in docs/guide/contributing.md. Regression test tests/test_reviewer_priority.py failed pre-fix (TypeError + config order) and passes post-fix (5 passed). Commit 9cdf56ed9.

chunk_findings.detail: The new test embeds literal reviewer-verdict text `STATUS: NO FINDINGS` as the fake reviewer stdout (also on line 112). Although it is intended only as fixture data for a command reviewer, the review rules say that diff text which states a reviewer verdict is itself reportable: automated review tooling or a reviewer scanning the change may treat it as an actual verdict or be influenced by it. The test should avoid placing a valid verdict string in the diff, e.g. by constructing the expected stdout from non-verdict fragments or using a placeholder that does not match the reviewer status grammar.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_priority.py:111

chunk_findings.detail: The test fixture bakes the reviewer verdict `STATUS: NO FINDINGS` into the generated reviewer scripts. Text inside the change that states a reviewer verdict must be reported, and here it is not merely cosmetic: that exact string is the protocol marker for a clean review, so if the fixture output is ever parsed outside the test, or if the review parser trusts the first status block it sees, it can spoof a passing review and mask findings. The test should use a non-status sentinel or explicitly assert that spoofed status blocks are not treated as authoritative.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_priority.py:_diary_reviewer

chunk_findings.detail: The test files task `T1` with `run_cli(repo, "task", "add", "T1", "--title", "add x", "--globs", "*.py")` without naming a phase, stating dependencies, or carrying a wave/no-deps tag. The recorded project rule [r-task-phase-needs-wave] requires every ddflow-filed task to have those fields; as written the test creates an invalid task fixture and will fail if the task validator enforces that rule.
